newsitem.title: UK: London gold prices static, platinum wobbly.
newsitem.headline: London gold prices static, platinum wobbly.

text.p: The gold market was very quiet early on Tuesday and prices were expected to meander in a tight range as business dries up ahead of the holidays.
Bullion was fixed at $368.30 an ounce, barely changed from Monday's afternoon fixing of $368.25.
Dealers and analysts pegged gold's near term price range at $367-$370 an ounce.
"Everything's winding down for Christmas. There's not much interbank trading and I can't see anything significant happening," a dealer said.
Gyrations in the jittery equities markets were having little noticable effect so far on the precious metals, as investors continued to stay away from gold.
A potentially market-moving hike in interest rates by the U.S. central bank's Federal Open Markets Committee on Tuesday was also considered unlikely by analysts.
"It would take something extraordinary to move the gold market," a dealer said.
"By now 50-point movements on Wall Street are run of the mill. The only way gold would rise in these short market conditions is a move in interest rates," he added.
Volatility was more likely in the platinum market, which came under pressure overnight when investors liquidated long positions in Tokyo.
Already at three-year lows, platinum looked increasingly wobbly, analysts said.
Price charts suggested a slide to the $365 support level was possible in the near term, said technical analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse.
Prices were little changed from Monday's weak London close, at $366.75/$367.75 an ounce.
"It's the one to watch because the trend is so bearish that there's a chance platinum could spike up on short covering," a dealer noted.
On the upside, platinum was expected to run into resistance at $370 and then at $372, dealers said.
Its sister metal palladium, indicated at $117.25/$118.25 was unchanged from Friday's London close.
Silver, like gold, was virtually static and seen wedged in a tight range. It was indicated at $4.80/$4.82 an ounce, up one cent from Monday's London close.
